_comment: TEMPLATE. Copy to `gateway/bifrost.json` (gitignored) and add the providers your
suite pins:
cp gateway/bifrost.example.json gateway/bifrost.json
Bifrost config for the benchmark's model plane (D5, ARCH §3, §6.1). Every LLM and
embedder call — harness and system under test alike — goes through here. Model pinning
is enforced per virtual key via provider_configs.allowed_models, provisioned at run
start by orchestrator/gateway.py; a non-pinned model gets a 403 model_blocked.
Provider keys are read from the environment and never inlined. `bench gateway start`
reads this file for the `env.*` names it references and reports any that are unset, by
name only — so a missing credential surfaces before a run rather than as a 401 mid-judge.
A provider is a base URL plus a credential, so a pinned model does not have to be an
OpenAI one. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, TGI, Ollama, Together, Groq,
OpenRouter, a private deployment) becomes a provider by adding a block with
network_config.base_url and custom_provider_config.base_provider_type: openai.
Field names verified against core/schemas/provider.go, not from the docs site.
One provider block per endpoint. The models listed on a key are what that key may
reach; the suite pins which (provider, id) pairs a run is allowed to use at all.
The two blocks below cover suites v1 and v2 (all `openai`) and LoCoMo-Refined's
official_judge (`qwen3-14b` on `vllm`). Suites v3 and v4 pin every model against a
private OpenAI-compatible deployment, which is deliberately absent here: add your own
block, name it in the suite, and note that changing a provider is a suite version bump
(ARCH §6.1) because the endpoint is part of the pinned environment.
Serves LoCoMo-Refined's official judge (qwen3-14b), which no OpenAI endpoint has.
`vllm` is a first-class Bifrost provider, so the endpoint is per-key under
vllm_key_config.url — a SecretVar, hence env.* works and the URL never sits in
this file. Prefer this over a custom provider: one key per instance also gives
round-robin across replicas, keyed on model_name.
For an endpoint that is not vLLM/Ollama, add a custom provider instead:
network_config.base_url (a plain string — NO env.* substitution here, so an
env.FOO is sent verbatim and the request silently goes nowhere)
custom_provider_config.base_provider_type: openai
custom_provider_config.is_key_less: true for an unauthenticated endpoint
custom_provider_config.request_path_overrides when it does not serve
/v1/chat/completions
base_url carries NO /v1 suffix. Bifrost appends the version prefix itself, so a
/v1 here resolves to /v1/v1/chat/completions and 404s on the first call.
Models are listed explicitly rather than as ["*"]. A wildcard would make every
virtual key's allowed_models unenforceable, which is the D11 bug.
